in_urdu.name: بہداد

historical_references.reference: The name Behdad first appeared during the Rashidun Caliphate, specifically during the caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab (634-644 AD). It was the name given to a significant agricultural oasis and settlement in the Syrian Desert, providing vital resources to the expanding Muslim army.

Later, during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 AD), Behdad became an important center for agricultural production and trade, especially in dates and textiles. It was one of the major cities of the Jazira region and a significant contributor to the prosperity of the Abbasid Empire.
